label: TSMM to GTR GRID/DIA binding
description: Maps Global Trust Registry, Global Registrar Information Directory, and Digital Identity Anchor concepts to TSMM trust-system primitives for authority, discovery, evidence, lifecycle, verification, decision receipts, and operational effects.

guarantees.name: bounded-authority-mapping
guarantees.description: Authoritative Registrars, GRID governance actors, and relying parties are mapped as TSMM actors with explicit scope, policy, and evidence obligations.

guarantees.name: discovery-to-decision-continuity
guarantees.description: GRID discovery artifacts can be carried forward into DIA verification and relying-party decision receipts.

guarantees.name: lifecycle-and-revocation-surfacing
guarantees.description: Registrar, GRID record, key, endpoint, and DIA state changes are represented as lifecycle events. Ecosystem-specific propagation timing remains a profile obligation.

limitations.name: not-a-gtr-conformance-claim
limitations.impact: This binding does not certify that a GRID or DIA implementation satisfies GTR operating requirements.
limitations.mitigation: Use this binding as a modeling and assurance scaffold, then attach GTR-specific conformance tests and policy references.

limitations.name: legal-authority-is-evidence-backed-not-inferred
limitations.impact: A listed GRID record cannot by itself prove legal authority unless supporting mandate evidence is present and in scope.
limitations.mitigation: Require authority evidence references in registrar admission, metadata publication, and relying-party verification receipts.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Admission into GRID should produce an auditable authority, scope, evidence, and lifecycle record, not merely a directory entry.
A verifier should bind signature validation to GRID discovery, registrar scope, lifecycle state, key state, revocation state, and relying-party policy before allowing an operational effect.
Withdrawal, suspension, key compromise, or revoked registrar authority should alter downstream discovery and relying decisions before new effects are admitted.

mappings.description: Models the overall institutional and technical trust domain for authoritative registrar discovery and DIA-based verification.
GRID maps to a curated trust-registry and discovery surface for registrar metadata, verification material, and lifecycle status.

mappings.externalConcept: GRID Board or administering UN body
mappings.description: Governance body that defines eligibility, technical standards, operating rules, and approval or suspension pathways.
Operational component that harvests, validates, publishes, and preserves registrar metadata under governance constraints.
A registrar is an issuer only within a bounded legal mandate, register scope, jurisdiction, lifecycle state, and GRID eligibility policy.
Entity whose legal registration claims and DID binding are represented by a DIA.
DIA maps to a credential artifact carrying registrar-issued identity claims and DID binding evidence.

mappings.externalConcept: Registrar legal mandate and eligibility criteria
mappings.description: Legal basis, eligibility criteria, participation level, and permitted register scope constrain what GRID recognition and DIA issuance can mean.

mappings.externalConcept: GRID record, signed metadata, public key, DID document, status response
mappings.description: Discovery and verification materials are evidence artifacts that support authority, key control, endpoint integrity, freshness, and lifecycle checks.
Actor that consumes GRID and DIA evidence to decide whether a business, compliance, or supply-chain effect should be admitted.
The output of applying relying-party and GTR policies to the DIA, GRID entry, authority scope, key state, revocation state, and evidence set.

mappings.externalConcept: Supplier onboarding, transaction approval, warning, downgrade, rejection, or manual review
mappings.description: Operational consequence admitted or blocked after the trust decision.

notes: This binding treats GRID recognition as a discovery and transparency signal, not as a certification of national legal status.
The binding is intentionally effect-centered: a verifier should evaluate whether the discovered and verified material is sufficient for a specific relying-party effect.
Participation maturity can be profiled from baseline listing through signed harvested data to DIA issuance and status automation.
Use for modeling, crosswalk, and assurance-design work while GTR implementation and operating rules continue to mature.
